questions.stem: A Dataflow Gen2 must read from a SQL Server running in your own datacentre, which is not reachable from the public internet. What has to be in place before the connection can be created?
options: An on-premises data gateway
A OneLake shortcut to the server
A workspace identity
A managed private endpoint on the lakehouse
questions.explanation: Fabric reaches sources inside a private network through an on-premises data gateway, which is installed on a machine that can see the source and registered in the tenant. Shortcuts point at cloud storage rather than a database server, and neither a workspace identity nor a lakehouse endpoint provides network connectivity to on-premises hardware.

questions.stem: Several pipelines and dataflows in different workspaces all read from the same Azure SQL Database. What is the benefit of defining the connection once at tenant level rather than inside each item?
options: Credentials are stored and rotated in one place, and the connection can be reused and shared
The data is cached centrally, so each item reads it faster
It converts the source into a Delta table automatically
It removes the need for any permissions on the source
questions.answer: Credentials are stored and rotated in one place, and the connection can be reused and shared
questions.explanation: Connections are managed objects with their own credentials and sharing model. Defining one centrally means a credential change happens once instead of in every item, and other creators can be granted use of the connection without ever seeing the secret. It does not cache data, convert formats, or remove the need for source-side permissions.

questions.stem: A colleague can see a connection listed in Fabric but cannot use it in their own dataflow. What is the most likely cause?
options: They have not been granted a role on the connection itself
The connection is bound to a different capacity
Connections can only ever be used by their creator
The connection needs to be re-created in each workspace
questions.answer: They have not been granted a role on the connection itself
questions.explanation: A connection carries its own permissions, separate from the workspace. Being able to see that a connection exists is not the same as being allowed to use it; the owner has to share it. Connections are not tied to a capacity, are shareable rather than private to their creator, and do not need duplicating per workspace.

questions.stem: You need to find streaming and event sources that already exist anywhere in your tenant, and subscribe to one of them. Which experience is designed for that?
options: Real-Time hub
OneLake catalog
Deployment pipelines
The Monitoring hub
questions.explanation: Real-Time hub is the tenant-wide place to discover streams and events and to subscribe to them. The OneLake catalog discovers data items rather than live streams, deployment pipelines move content between stages, and the Monitoring hub shows the status of runs.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Discover data by using OneLake catalog and Real-Time hub

questions.stem: An analyst wants to find a trustworthy semantic model about sales without knowing which workspace it lives in. Where should they start?
options: The OneLake catalog, filtering by endorsement
The admin portal tenant settings
The workspace list, opening each one in turn
The Real-Time hub
questions.answer: The OneLake catalog, filtering by endorsement
questions.explanation: The OneLake catalog is the tenant-wide view of data items a user can reach, and it surfaces endorsement so trustworthy items stand out. Walking the workspace list only shows workspaces they already belong to, tenant settings are an administrative surface, and Real-Time hub is for streams and events.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Discover data by using OneLake catalog and Real-Time hub

questions.stem: Which endorsement level signals that an item has been reviewed against your organisation's quality standards by an authorised reviewer, rather than simply recommended by its owner?
options: Certified
Promoted
Featured
Published
questions.explanation: Promotion is self-service: any contributor can promote an item they consider ready. Certification is a controlled step performed by reviewers an administrator has authorised, which is why it carries more weight when someone is deciding whether to trust a dataset they did not build.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Discover data by using OneLake catalog and Real-Time hub

questions.stem: A lakehouse needs to read Parquet files that already sit in an ADLS Gen2 account, with no transformation and without duplicating the storage. Which approach fits best?
options: Create a OneLake shortcut to the ADLS Gen2 location
Run a Copy activity on a schedule into the lakehouse Files area
Build a Dataflow Gen2 that loads the files into a table
Mount the account inside a notebook on every run
questions.answer: Create a OneLake shortcut to the ADLS Gen2 location
questions.explanation: A shortcut exposes external storage inside OneLake without copying it, so there is one copy of the data and no ingestion schedule to maintain. Copy activities and dataflows both move the bytes, which is what the requirement rules out, and mounting inside a notebook makes the data reachable only while that notebook runs.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Ingest or access data as needed

questions.stem: Which Fabric item gives a low-code, Power Query based experience for ingesting and reshaping data on the way in?
options: Dataflow Gen2
Data pipeline
Eventstream
Notebook
questions.explanation: Dataflow Gen2 is the Power Query experience: you connect, transform with the visual editor or M, and land the result. Pipelines orchestrate activities rather than transform rows, Eventstream handles streaming ingestion, and notebooks are code-first.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Ingest or access data as needed

questions.stem: A nightly load must copy files, then run a notebook, then refresh a semantic model, stopping if any step fails. Which item should orchestrate it?
options: A data pipeline
A Dataflow Gen2
A KQL queryset
A deployment pipeline
questions.explanation: Data pipelines exist to sequence activities with dependencies, conditions and retries, which is exactly what a multi-step nightly load needs. A dataflow performs one transformation job, a KQL queryset queries data, and a deployment pipeline promotes content between stages rather than running a workload.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Ingest or access data as needed

questions.stem: A team needs multi-table transactions and full T-SQL inserts, updates and deletes against their curated tables. Which Fabric store meets that requirement?
options: Warehouse
Lakehouse, through its SQL analytics endpoint
Eventhouse
A semantic model in Direct Lake mode
questions.explanation: The Warehouse supports full T-SQL DDL and DML with multi-table transactions. A lakehouse's SQL analytics endpoint is read-only, so writes have to go through Spark or a pipeline instead. Eventhouse is for high-volume telemetry queried with KQL, and a semantic model is a serving layer rather than a store you write to.

questions.stem: Which statement about a lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint is correct?
options: It serves T-SQL queries over the lakehouse tables but cannot be used to write to them
It supports the same inserts and updates as a warehouse
It replaces the need for Delta tables in the lakehouse
It is only available while a Spark session is running
questions.answer: It serves T-SQL queries over the lakehouse tables but cannot be used to write to them
questions.explanation: The SQL analytics endpoint gives a familiar T-SQL read surface over the lakehouse's Delta tables. It is read-only, which is the single most useful fact to know when choosing between a lakehouse and a warehouse. It does not replace Delta storage and does not depend on an open Spark session.

questions.stem: Billions of rows of device telemetry arrive continuously and analysts need sub-second time-series queries over them. Which store is designed for that shape of workload?
options: Eventhouse
Warehouse
Lakehouse
A Power BI import model
questions.explanation: Eventhouse is built for high-volume, high-velocity telemetry and log data, queried with KQL and optimised for time-series analysis. A warehouse or lakehouse can hold the data but is not tuned for that ingestion rate and query pattern, and an import model would have to be refreshed rather than queried live.

questions.stem: You enable OneLake availability on a KQL database. In what form does the data become available to the rest of Fabric?
options: As Delta Lake tables in OneLake, readable by other engines
As a read-only copy in an Azure Storage account you nominate
As a semantic model that refreshes on a schedule
As CSV extracts written on each ingestion batch
questions.answer: As Delta Lake tables in OneLake, readable by other engines
questions.explanation: OneLake availability surfaces the Eventhouse data as Delta Lake tables in OneLake, so Spark, T-SQL and semantic models can read the same logical copy without a separate export. That is the point of the feature: one copy, many engines.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement OneLake integration for Eventhouse and semantic models

questions.stem: Which semantic model storage mode reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, without importing the data and without sending queries to a SQL endpoint?
options: Direct Lake
Import
DirectQuery
Dual
questions.explanation: Direct Lake loads Delta Parquet files from OneLake straight into the engine's memory, so there is neither a scheduled import nor a per-query round trip to a relational source. Import copies the data, DirectQuery translates every query to the source, and Dual is a per-table combination of Import and DirectQuery.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement OneLake integration for Eventhouse and semantic models

questions.stem: A report on a Direct Lake semantic model must reflect telemetry captured in an Eventhouse minutes ago, without anyone running a refresh. Which combination achieves that?
options: Enable OneLake availability on the KQL database and build the Direct Lake model over the resulting Delta tables
Export the KQL results to CSV and import them into the model each morning
Point the model at the Eventhouse with DirectQuery and disable caching
Schedule an incremental refresh every minute
questions.answer: Enable OneLake availability on the KQL database and build the Direct Lake model over the resulting Delta tables
questions.explanation: OneLake availability keeps the Eventhouse data present as Delta tables, and Direct Lake reads those files directly, so newly landed data is visible without an import step. Every other option reintroduces a copy or a scheduled refresh, which is exactly what the requirement excludes.
questions.sourceSkillBullet: Implement OneLake integration for Eventhouse and semantic models
